Phase: Phase 0 — Decision, architecture and logging
Name: Remote-access paths and residual VPN use inventoried (Network & Access N0.1)
Owner or approver: Executive sponsor and CIO (Network & Access Modernization plan)
If late (decisions): The adoption decision has no inventory of the VPN's applications and users to weigh

Phase: Phase 0 — Decision, architecture and logging
Name: Tenant licenses and onboarding state read; current VPN and SSE functions mapped to the four traffic types

Phase: Phase 0 — Decision, architecture and logging
Name: Adopt Global Secure Access, per function: Microsoft traffic, internet, private, branch
Owner or approver: Service owner, approved by the authorizing official
Options (decisions): Adopt the function; keep the current VPN or SSE for it; run both with each traffic type sent to one service. Recorded with license count, availability quote, compensating controls and exit criteria
If late (decisions): No license count can be ordered, and the Network plan's egress decision (D-N5) can't weigh agent-delivered SASE

Phase: Phase 0 — Decision, architecture and logging
Name: Egress pattern decided for each pilot site (Network & Access D-N5)
If late (decisions): The pilot sites' egress is chosen without knowing whether pattern D, agent-delivered SASE, is available

Phase: Phase 0 — Decision, architecture and logging
Name: Reference architecture recorded: profiles per population, connector groups, branch pattern; first configuration export with its hash manifest

Phase: Phase 0 — Decision, architecture and logging
Name: Network log categories exported by diagnostic setting; Sentinel solution installed; traffic-drop alert on; freshness query clean

Phase: Phase 0 — Decision, architecture and logging
Name: Gate 0 — Decided per function, logging before any pilot traffic
Criteria (gates): Decision record approved per function, with a license count no smaller than the pilot and first ring, an availability quote dated within 30 days and an approver; architecture record and the first configuration export with its hash manifest; the four network log categories reaching the workspace

Phase: Phase 1 — Client, Microsoft traffic and the pilot ring
Name: Client packaged as an Intune Win32 app with Learn's commands and detection rule; DoH off; ring 0, the implementing team

Phase: Phase 1 — Client, Microsoft traffic and the pilot ring
Name: Microsoft traffic profile on for ring 0; source IP restoration and Conditional Access signaling on; sign-in share measured

Phase: Phase 1 — Client, Microsoft traffic and the pilot ring
Name: Universal tenant restrictions (TRv2) policy approved, tagging on, four-case test recorded

Phase: Phase 1 — Client, Microsoft traffic and the pilot ring
Name: Conditional Access baseline enforced; emergency access accounts vaulted and tested (program P1.6)
If late (decisions): The compliant network policy has no tested emergency access exclusion, and its report-only run waits

Phase: Phase 1 — Client, Microsoft traffic and the pilot ring
Name: Compliant network policy in report-only for 10 business days; break-glass scripts staged

Phase: Phase 1 — Client, Microsoft traffic and the pilot ring
Name: Turn the compliant network policy On for ring 1
Options (decisions): On, ring by ring; stay in report-only until every reportOnlyFailure is explained
If late (decisions): Ring 1 runs without the network condition, and its exit waits

Phase: Phase 1 — Client, Microsoft traffic and the pilot ring
Name: Pilot Conditional Access and Intune policies assigned (program P2.2)
If late (decisions): The pilot cohort's devices can't take the client through Intune, and ring 1 waits

Phase: Phase 1 — Client, Microsoft traffic and the pilot ring
Name: Ring 1, fewer than 20 users across roles and sites: client, Microsoft traffic, TRv2 and compliant network for 10 business days; emergency access exclusion tested at ring start

Phase: Phase 1 — Client, Microsoft traffic and the pilot ring
Name: Gate 1 — Ring 1 exited on Microsoft traffic
Criteria (gates): Every step's Validate passed for ring 0 and break-glass rehearsed; ring 1 for 10 business days with no unresolved Sev-2 ticket; client active on every pilot device; report-only results clean; compliant network On for ring 1

Phase: Phase 2 — Private Access and administrative paths
Name: First private applications, and Quick Access as a bridge or per-app from the start
Options (decisions): Quick Access over the VPN's ranges as a transition, then per-app; per-app from the start for the VPN's most-used applications. DirectAccess can't coexist with Private Access on the same device
If late (decisions): Connector groups can't be sized or placed, and Private Access waits

Phase: Phase 2 — Private Access and administrative paths
Name: Connector groups deployed: two outbound-only connectors per group on Windows Server 2019 or later, TLS 1.2, no inline inspection; private DNS

Phase: Phase 2 — Private Access and administrative paths
Name: First private applications published per app with their own segments, assignment and Conditional Access, for ring 1; application discovery run

Phase: Phase 2 — Private Access and administrative paths
Name: Administrative hosts behind phishing-resistant policies; domain controller sensors moved from Audit to Enforce for application SPNs

Phase: Phase 2 — Private Access and administrative paths
Name: Gate 2 — Private applications per app for ring 1
Criteria (gates): Each published application has its own segments, group assignment and Conditional Access; Quick Access residual at zero for the moved applications; administrative hosts reachable only under phishing-resistant policies; sensors enforcing

Phase: Phase 3 — Internet Access and TLS inspection
Name: Web categories the acceptable-use policy blocks
Options (decisions): Block the categories the acceptable-use policy names; decide AI categories separately; every bypass to the exception register
If late (decisions): Security profiles can't be built, and Internet Access waits

Phase: Phase 3 — Internet Access and TLS inspection
Name: Security profiles with web content filtering and threat intelligence, linked by Conditional Access for ring 1; the baseline profile last

Phase: Phase 3 — Internet Access and TLS inspection
Name: TLS inspection scope and its certificate authority
Owner or approver: Service owner, approved by the privacy officer
Options (decisions): Microsoft-managed certificate; the agency's own intermediate signed by a dedicated CA, not the production PKI. Learn's recommended bypass categories kept, plus those the privacy officer names; no prompt or file content capture without a separate decision
If late (decisions): Inspection can't start, URL and file rules stay unavailable, and Gate 3 waits

Phase: Phase 3 — Internet Access and TLS inspection
Name: Inspection intermediate signed; root and intermediate trusted on pilot devices by Intune profile; user notice sent

Phase: Phase 3 — Internet Access and TLS inspection
Name: TLS inspection on for the pilot security profile; pinned applications bypassed; failure rate measured

Phase: Phase 3 — Internet Access and TLS inspection
Name: Gate 3 — Internet traffic filtered and inspected for ring 1
Criteria (gates): Security profiles with web filtering and threat intelligence; bypasses in the exception register; TLS inspection from a dedicated CA with the privacy officer's approval and user notice; TLS failure rate under 1%

Phase: Phase 4 — Rings 2 and 3, and the VPN's retirement
Name: Client hardening from ring 2: Disable hidden, non-privileged users restricted, help desk elevation path

Phase: Phase 4 — Rings 2 and 3, and the VPN's retirement
Name: Ring 2, about 10% of users including one branch, for 20 business days, every function at once

Phase: Phase 4 — Rings 2 and 3, and the VPN's retirement
Name: CISA telemetry path for the new access layer, agreed with the TIC delegates
Owner or approver: ISSO, with the agency's TIC delegates
Options (decisions): CLAW; another path CISA confirms. Agreed before the VPN's web path is retired
If late (decisions): The VPN's web path can't be retired, and Gate 4 waits

Phase: Phase 4 — Rings 2 and 3, and the VPN's retirement
Name: Program starts rollout wave 1 (start of P3.1)
If late (decisions): Ring 3 has no divisions to follow

Phase: Phase 4 — Rings 2 and 3, and the VPN's retirement
Name: Ring 3, everyone in scope in waves with the program's divisions; each wave on the ring 2 criteria

Phase: Phase 4 — Rings 2 and 3, and the VPN's retirement
Name: VPN routes removed per application after 10 business days with no VPN traffic; the VPN's web path retired; residual VPN use in the exception register

Phase: Phase 4 — Rings 2 and 3, and the VPN's retirement
Name: Zero Trust Assessment rerun; each network finding's closure chain updated with evidence for every applicable state

Phase: Phase 4 — Rings 2 and 3, and the VPN's retirement
Name: Gate 4 — Every ring exited, evidence complete
Criteria (gates): Each ring exited on its recorded criteria with measured values; VPN routes removed only after each wave held; CISA telemetry agreed; emergency access exclusion tested at each ring start; evidence package for each finding ready for the assessor (closure is the authorizing official's decision)
